editorial:
Imagine your life is already tough, and then a giant rock from space crashes right into your backyard. That is exactly what happens to this Irish family. You get to follow a group of siblings who are struggling to get by after losing their parents. When the meteor hits, the kids are convinced it is a sign or a gift from their parents in heaven. It gives them a spark of hope and a reason to believe in something bigger. The movie feels grounded and real, blending a bit of crime and family drama with a strange, sci-fi twist that keeps you guessing about what the rock actually means for their future.

The acting is the best part here because the chemistry between the siblings feels natural and honest. You will love how the story balances sad moments with the tension of the government trying to take their prize away. While some parts of the plot move a bit slow, the payoff is worth it. If you are in the mood for a heartfelt story about family and faith, you should definitely check this out. Since it is an older gem, you might want to look for a 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best quality, or just rent it on Apple TV for a cozy movie night.
endingExplained: After the government and university experts take the meteor, the family realizes the rock was not a magical gift but a catalyst for change. They stop obsessing over the object and start focusing on each other. The movie ends with the siblings finally finding peace with their parents' death. They learn that the real miracle was the way the event brought them closer together, allowing them to heal and move forward as a family.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family dramas with a touch of mystery.
